description:
On August 1, 1966, Charles Whitman opened fire from the University of Texas Tower in Austin, Texas. For 96 terrifying minutes, the Texas Tower sniper shooting brought an entire campus to a standstill and became one of the most infamous mass shootings in American history.

But what drove Charles Whitman to carry out the 1966 University of Texas Tower shooting? And could the warning signs have prevented the tragedy?

In this true crime documentary, we uncover the disturbing story behind the Texas Tower sniper rampage. From Whitman's troubled childhood and military background to his deteriorating mental state, chilling warnings, and the horrific events of August 1, 1966, we reconstruct the attack that shocked America.

Discover how the shooting unfolded, how Austin police officers Ramiro Martinez and Houston McCoy confronted the gunman, and why the discovery of a brain tumor during Whitman's autopsy left investigators with troubling unanswered questions.

We also explore how the 1966 Texas Tower massacre exposed serious weaknesses in law enforcement and helped shape the development of modern SWAT teams.
